For training, we adopt reciprocal learning (Lacroix et al., 2018), in which we add an inverse triple $(t,r^{-1},h)$ for each observed triple $(h,r,t)$ in the training data. For model optimization, we use Ada-grad (Duchi et al., 2011) as the optimizer, and employ grid search to find the best hyperparameters according to their performances on validation sets. The hyperparameters we search over includes embedding size ( $\{128,256,512,1024\}$ ), batch size ( $\{300,500,1000,2000,5000\}$ ), learning rate ( $\{0.1,0.01\}$ ), and regularization parameters of Equation 12 ( $\lambda:\{0,5\mathrm{e} - 3,1\mathrm{e} - 2,5\mathrm{e} - 2,7\mathrm{e} - 2,1\mathrm{e} - 1,1.5\mathrm{e} - 1\}$ ; $\lambda_1,\lambda_2:\{0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0\}$ ). The parameters used in Table 2 are shown in Table 7. We implement our BiQUE model in PyTorch, and run all experiments on NVIDIA Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs. Table 7: Best hyperparameters for benchmarks. Lr is learning rate. $\lambda, \lambda_1, \lambda_2$ are Equation 12's hyperparameters.
